sentences.text: Why does a geyser suddenly launch boiling water into the air? Is Earth making tea, or having a plumbing crisis?
Groundwater seeps through cracks and gets heated by hot rock. But heat alone isn't enough. The underground plumbing matters too.
Deep underground, high pressure can keep water liquid even above its boiling temperature at the surface.
Steam bubbles can collect behind narrow passages. When bubbling pushes some water out, pressure in the system drops.
That pressure drop lets more hot water flash into steam. The expanding steam drives hot water out in an eruption.
The eruption stops when the system cools or runs short of water. Water can refill the plumbing, and the cycle starts again.
So, is a geyser nature's pressure cooker... or the world's least relaxing water fountain?
